transitions.label: 7s 2[3/2]°2 - 7p 2[5/2]3 (745.0 nm air)
transitions.use: the line of the only laser-spectroscopy study of radon: collinear fast-beam laser spectroscopy at ISOLDE (Borchers, Neugart, Otten et al., Hyperfine Interact. 34, 25 (1987)): isotope shifts between 16 isotopes in the range 202-222Rn and hyperfine structure of 7 odd-A isotopes, per the abstract.
transitions.note: hyperfine A and B constants of both levels for 203m, 205, 207, 209, 211, 219, 221Rn are stored under the two levels (Borchers et al., Table 1). The isotope shifts of 16 isotopes (202-212, 218-222Rn, relative to 212Rn) are shown only as a graph (Fig. 3 of the paper: about +8.5 GHz at A = 202 falling to 0 at 212 and to about -23 GHz at A = 222, nu(A) - nu(212)); the paper prints no numerical isotope shifts, so none are stored.

conflicts: Magnetic moments: the 'preliminary' values printed by Borchers et al. 1987 (e.g. 207Rn 0.80, 203mRn -0.94 n.m., 5 % accuracy) differ slightly from the evaluated IAEA-table values stored under 'isotopes' (207Rn 0.8124(16)); the IAEA values are kept there. For A = 203 the IAEA entry is the ground state (I = 3/2) whereas the laser measurement is on the I = 13/2 isomer (hyperfine key '203m').
not_found: numerical isotope shifts of the 745 nm line: Borchers et al. (Hyperfine Interact. 34, 25 (1987), opened as CERN-EP/86-191) give them only as a graph (Fig. 3), no table; a later full paper or the thesis with the numbers was not located (INSPIRE lists only this conference contribution; CERN document server is behind a bot wall). The hyperfine constants of Table 1 are now stored.
radiative lifetimes of any Rn I level (7s, 7p, 6d): no measurement found; no calculated values found either (two web searches, arXiv and INSPIRE queries)
transition probabilities / oscillator strengths of the 178.6 nm and 145.2 nm resonance lines and of the 7s-7p near-infrared lines: none found; NIST ASD lists none
lifetime of the metastable 7s 2[3/2]°2 level: none found
precise (laser) frequencies of any Rn I line: none found; all wavelengths are the classical discharge-spectrum values that NIST uses
measured ionization energy more recent than the NIST value 86692.5 cm^-1: none found
notes: Radon is the least-studied of these atoms: apart from the classical emission spectra there is a single collinear-laser-spectroscopy study (ISOLDE, published 1987) on the 745 nm line, whose hyperfine constants were read in the third pass (2026-10-02) from the CERN preprint scan of the conference paper (data/literature/pdf/Rn_Borchers_1987.pdf); its isotope shifts exist only as a graph. Nuclear spins, half-lives and moments are taken from the IAEA table; moments printed there for even-even isotopes belong to isomers and were left out. The site's default isotope (222Rn) has I = 0, so no hyperfine structure applies to it.
